newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Southcorp launches wine cork alternative.
newsitem.headline: Southcorp launches wine cork alternative.

text.p: Wine and packaging group Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Monday its packaging division had launched a synthetic wine bottle closure, an alternative to the standard cork, which could put an end to cork taint.

Southcorp Packaging executive general manager Barry Watts said the company anticipated the product would gain, over time, a significant share of the world market for closures for commercial wines - table wines priced at the lower end of the price spectrum which form the bulk of retail purchases.
"This market is estimated at nine billion units, worth as much as A$70 million per annum, including 150 million units in Australia and New Zealand alone," he said in a statement.

Watts said Southcorp's synthetic closure Aegis, which had the look and feel of natural cork, could be run on existing bottling lines, was removed from the bottle with a standard corkscrew and was recyclable.

With cork taint estimated to affect 1.4 billion bottles of wine around the world each year, Aegis was the first synethetic closure to offer winemakers a competitively priced, taint-free, consistent protection against leakage and oxidation, he said.
"Synthetic closures are becoming increasingly accepted in the United Kingdom and other countries around the world," Watts said.

The statement said that following a successful trial the division's sister company Southcorp Wines, Australia's largest wine producer, would be its first customer, with plans for introducing the product with an initial run over one million bottles of commercial wines.
